author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: I need the risk assessment for the allocation logic to pass through a formal compliance review before we approve the acceptance criteria. The supplier has already confirmed the bulk order for next week, so the physical stock is locked in. If the allocation logic misses a compliance gap, we are left holding pallets that cannot be legally distributed. I want this review to be as thorough as possible. The more eyes we put on the validation steps, the safer the system is. I am not asking for a quick glance. I need a deep, formal sign off that proves every edge case in the allocation math is handled correctly. This level of scrutiny is the only way I can feel confident that the automated process is ready to handle committed inventory without breaking any rules.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that they want the review to be as thorough as possible and that more scrutiny makes the system safer, indicating that exceeding the minimum requirement of a formal sign-off would increase their satisfaction and confidence.
